title: Smoked Potato Salad Tray
seoTitle: Smoked Potato Salad Tray | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Cold side with smoke depth that pairs with every protein on the pit
subtitle: Smoked potatoes, tangy mustard dressing, and herbs for ten
description: Adapted from classic BBQ potato salad tradition (Weber, Hey Grill Hey): Yukon golds smoke at 250°F until tender, get diced, and fold into a tangy mustard-mayo dressing for a tray that feeds ten.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Smoked Potato Salad Tray in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use neutral oil, mayonnaise as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch vegetarian. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Prep potatoes
steps.instruction: Halve potatoes, toss with oil, salt, and pepper. Arrange cut-side down on sheet pans. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Smoke at 250°F
steps.instruction: Smoke potatoes at 250°F until fork-tender and internal temp reaches 205°F, about 60–75 minutes. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Cool and dice
steps.instruction: Cool potatoes 20 minutes until warm, not hot. Dice into 1/2-inch cubes. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Build dressing
steps.instruction: Whisk mayo, mustard, vinegar, and pinch of salt until smooth. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Fold salad
steps.instruction: Fold potatoes with dressing, celery, onion, pickles, dill, and eggs if using. taste and adjust salt, acid, and pepper until balanced.

steps.title: Chill for service
steps.instruction: Refrigerate at least 30 minutes so flavors meld. Keep on ice at the line. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

steps.title: Cooking step
steps.instruction: Potato salad in a cold pan on ice alongside smoked meats. Refresh with dill before serving. Target 165°F for any egg-based components at the thickest part before moving to the next batch. Plan about 3 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Leftovers
steps.instruction: Keeps refrigerated 24 hours. Thin with vinegar if dressing tightens overnight. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: 205°F internal on potatoes means creamy center after dice.
Dress while potatoes are warm—they absorb flavor better.
Keep cold: this is the relief side on a hot smoke board.
tonightSpread: Smoked potato salad in a cold tray on ice.
Extra dill and cracked pepper for finishing.
leftovers: Loaded potato salad bowls with chopped brisket.
Spread on grilled bread for a smoky picnic toast.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Potato salad is the cold anchor on a hot smoke board. Smoked spuds add depth without weirdness, and it holds refrigerated 24 hours.
mealPrepNotes: Smoke potatoes ahead—they need to cool before dressing. Keep finished salad cold on ice until service. Do not hold warm.
